rules.rule: Python `^` is start-of-string only (no /m by default); `.` does not match '\n' but DOES match '\r'. Inline flags (?s), (?m), (?x), (?a), (?i) work but ONLY at the very start of the pattern — a mid-pattern global flag is a re.error and crashes.

rules.rule: \d, \w, \s are FULL-UNICODE by default (Python str patterns are re.UNICODE). \d matches Arabic-Indic and fullwidth digits, \w matches accented letters, \s matches NBSP and EM SPACE. (?a) restores ASCII-only. JS \d/\w are ASCII-only, so a translator must expand these classes.
Regex operates on CODE POINTS: '.' matches a whole astral character and a character class may contain an astral literal. Equivalent to JS RegExp with the /u flag.
(?i) uses Python's Unicode simple case folding: 'K' (U+212A KELVIN SIGN) matches /k/i, but 'ß' does NOT match 'ss'.

Python-only regex syntax that must be supported: named group (?P<x>...), backreference (?P=x), numeric backreference \1, conditional (?(1)a|b), comment group (?#...), \A, \Z, bare ']' and bare '{' as literals, POSIX-looking [[:alpha:]] treated as an ordinary character class (NOT a POSIX class), and possessive quantifiers a*+ (Python 3.11+).

Syntax that is a re.error in Python (=> EMPTY, exit 1) even though JS accepts some of it: JS-style named group (?<x>...), \z, \g<1>, \Q...\E, \p{L}, variable-width lookbehind, atomic group (?>...) is accepted-but-different, leading '*', 'a**', unterminated '[' or '('.

rules.rule: `$schema` inside the schema is ignored — the validator is always Draft7 and check_schema always uses the Draft7 metaschema.
Unknown keywords are ignored silently (no error, no schema error). maxLength:0 on '""' passes; on '"a"' fails.
Malformed JSON in either --a or --b => json.JSONDecodeError, EMPTY stdout, exit 1. Missing --a or --b => argparse usage message on stderr, EMPTY stdout, exit 2.

rules.rule: Duplicate JSON object keys: last one wins (Python json.loads semantics), same as JS JSON.parse.
Applicator keywords each produce exactly ONE error at the instance path (their subschema errors are nested as context, not counted): anyOf, oneOf, not, if/then all give raw count 1.

surprises: Line 1 vs line 2 diverge whenever two errors share (absolute path, keyword). The classic trigger is allOf with repeated keywords: --a '"ab"' --b '{"allOf":[{"minLength":3},{"minLength":4},{"minLength":5}]}' prints 1,3,3,False,False,False,None,None,1,1. Nested version --a '["a","b"]' --b '{"items":{"allOf":[{"minLength":3},{"minLength":4}]}}' prints 2,4,4,...,2,2.
minLength/maxLength count Python code points, so JS str.length is wrong for any astral char. '😀😀' is length 2, not 4.

Python `$` matches before a single trailing newline: pattern '^abc$' VALIDATES the string "abc
". JS would reject. But '' and '
' are not exempt, and '

' is not exempt.
\d, \w, \s are Unicode-aware: '٣' and '１' match ^\d$, 'é' matches ^\w$, NBSP/EM-SPACE match ^\s$. A naive JS port using the same source string gets all four backwards.

`format` is completely inert during validation (no format_checker), yet check_schema DOES enforce format 'regex' on `pattern` values and `patternProperties` keys. So {"format":"email"} never errors, but {"pattern":"["} kills the whole program.

An invalid regex ANYWHERE in the schema — including inside `definitions` or a branch the instance never reaches, and even when the instance is a number — aborts everything with empty stdout and exit 1, because check_schema walks the entire schema.
Non-integer/negative/boolean minLength (3.5, -1, true) crash via check_schema, but integer-valued floats (3.0, 1e2) are perfectly legal and behave as integers.
A STRING minLength value crashes only if the instance is a string (TypeError inside the keyword), otherwise it crashes later inside check_schema — different traceback, identical observable output.
[[:alpha:]] is NOT a POSIX class in Python; it is a character class of the literals [ : a l p h and does not match 'a'.
Python-only regex constructs like (?P<x>...), (?P=x), (?(1)a|b), (?#...), \A, \Z, and possessive a*+ are legal; JS-only forms (?<x>...), \z, \g<1>, \p{L}, variable-width lookbehind are hard errors.
Mid-pattern global inline flags such as 'a(?i)bc' are a re.error in modern Python, so they crash instead of validating.
(?>a*)ab is an atomic group in Python 3.11+ and therefore does NOT match "aab" (1 error), unlike a plain (a*)ab which would.
Schema values `true`/`false` are valid schemas, but `null`, a string, or an array as the schema crash with AttributeError/TypeError.
